![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14119854/assets/4d1c20f44c7a092275f200737813e11c762e1f3e80ba22ded29b41731e22472e.png)

Calculate ${\int }_{C}\,\text{d}x,$ where $C={C}_{1}\cup {C}_{2}$ is the path comprising of two line segments, as shown above.
question.worked_solution:
The line integral of unity with respect to $x$ along a path $C$ is equal to the net change in $x$ between the terminal and initial points:

$$
{\int }_{C}\,\text{d}x={x}_{2}-{x}_{1},
$$

where ${x}_{2}$ is the $x$-coordinate of the terminal point, and ${x}_{1}$ is the $x$-coordinate of the initial point.

In our case, ${x}_{2}=4$ and ${x}_{1}=0.$ Therefore,

$$
{\int }_{C}\,\text{d}x={x}_{2}-{x}_{1}=4-0=4.
$$
